newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Nat jumps on bid speculation.
newsitem.headline: Cr Nat jumps on bid speculation.

text.p: French bank Credit National surged 7.75 percent to 304 francs by 1055 GMT on market speculation that it could become a bid target.
"People are speculating. There are rumours it could become a bid target. And when you look at its re-evaluated net asset worth, it's around 500 to 550 francs per share," one Paris dealer said.
The buying was fuelled by a news report in the financial daily La Tribune which suggested that French banks BNP or Credit Commercial de France might be interested in Credit National.
The share gained 1.7 percent on Tuesday. Credit National, which has been declaring for some time that its share is undervalued, said last month it believed it was open to a takeover.

"This is the second time this fall we've had this kind of bid speculation," said one banking analyst. "It makes sense Credit National should be a takeover target as its share is trading below book value, but I really don't see who would buy it."
"It doesn't make sense that BNP or CCF would want to extend their activities in that fashion," he said.

"Credit National has no real market of its own, it has been made fragile by losses and management problems," said another analyst. "It's logical someone would buy it as they would get around three billion francs worth of shareholders funds."

Credit National's shares have been climbing after falling to a year low of 226 francs on October 24. The decline followed disappointment at its half-year results in which the bank plunged to a loss of 112 million francs compared with a profit of 236 million francs for the year-earlier period.
The loss reflected a restructuring charge to cover its merger with Banque Francaise de Commerce Exterieur.
